overview: A remarkably active day on bpf-next dominated by two landmark series: Alexei Starovoitov posted both a new indirect call instruction (callx) enabling function-pointer-style dispatch between BPF subprograms, and a verifier overhaul that verifies loops by widening scalars at loop heads rather than walking every iteration. Kumar Kartikeya Dwivedi followed with a v2 of his 18-patch series raising the BPF program stack limit from 512 bytes to 2 KiB.

patches.title: bpf: Add callx instruction to call bpf subprogs indirectly
patches.author: Alexei Starovoitov
patches.summary: Introduces the new BPF callx instruction, which dispatches to a BPF subprogram through a register containing a function pointer. This enables C-style indirect calls and virtual-dispatch patterns inside BPF programs, a capability that was previously impossible without helper indirection. The series accompanies callx with x86 and arm64 JIT backends, verifier recognition of read-only map pointers to functions, and libbpf support for resolving function pointers in read-only data sections. Documentation for the new ISA instruction is included as the final patch.

patches.title: bpf: Widen scalars at loop heads
patches.author: Alexei Starovoitov
patches.summary: Core patch in an 8-patch series that fundamentally changes how the BPF verifier handles loops by widening scalar ranges at detected loop-head instructions instead of re-walking every iteration. This eliminates the exponential blow-up that forced many programs to use bpf_loop() or may_goto workarounds and dramatically reduces verification time for programs with bounded iterator patterns. Companion patches detect loop heads during check_cfg(), handle loops that never exit, and automatically insert may_goto annotations for loops that cannot be fully bounded.

patches.title: bpf, x86: Allow programs 2 KiB of stack
patches.author: Kumar Kartikeya Dwivedi
patches.summary: Part of a v2 18-patch series raising the BPF program stack limit from the historical 512-byte ceiling to 2 KiB on both x86 and arm64 JIT backends. To support this safely the series reworks the verifier to track scratched and backtracking stack slots with bitmaps (replacing fixed-width arrays), dynamically sizes liveness masks per frame, and introduces a per-program stack budget enforced at load time. The size increase unlocks more complex BPF programs that previously required map-based scratch space.

patches.title: btf: Extend UAPI to support BTF location (inline site) info
patches.author: Alan Maguire
patches.summary: First patch in a v4 11-patch series that adds three new BTF kinds — BTF_KIND_LOC, BTF_KIND_LOC_PARAM, and BTF_KIND_LOCSEC — encoding the source location (file, line, column) and call-site context of inlined functions. This fills a longstanding gap where BPF stack traces and error messages could not name the inline frames responsible for a given instruction. The series adds libbpf encoding and decoding support, bpftool dump commands, distill/dedup handling, and kernel documentation.

patches.title: bpf: tcp: Introduce bpf_tcp_ops.{enqueue,dequeue}_rcvq()
patches.author: Kuniyuki Iwashima
patches.summary: Core patch in the v2 TCP AutoLOWAT series, adding two new BPF struct-ops hooks that fire when data is enqueued to or dequeued from a TCP socket's receive queue. Combined with a new bpf_tcp_set_rcvlowat() kfunc (patch 7/8) this lets a BPF program dynamically tune sk_rcvlowat per-socket, reducing unnecessary epoll wakeups under bursty workloads. The series also converts the bpf_{get,set}sockopt() deny-list to an allow-list for better safety.

patches.title: bpf: Fix arena race between page free and alloc leading to incoherency
patches.author: Emil Tsalapatis
patches.summary: Addresses a race in the BPF arena VM fault handler where a concurrent free and allocation of the same page could leave the range tree and the PTE in inconsistent states, causing silent memory corruption. The fix makes PTE installation and range-tree updates atomic and introduces an explicit state machine for free spans. Two earlier patches in the series (v3) improve range-tree availability tracking and fix the is_range_tree_set helper for consecutive-range checks.

patches.title: libbpf: BPF programs manual loading and attaching
patches.author: Andrey Grodzovsky
patches.summary: Key patch in a v5 8-patch libbpf series adding a BPF_PROG_LOAD_STRATEGY_MANUAL mode that defers a program's kernel load and attachment to user-controlled calls, rather than having bpf_object__load() do it automatically. This is useful for tools like veristat that need to control load order or inspect programs before loading. The series also introduces a declarative SEC("!...") prefix syntax, versions the bpf_program__set_autoattach() ABI change, and converts veristat to the new API.
